episode_title: 125. The illusion of progress | Why multitasking is destroying your productivity

real_qa.q: Why is driving while using a cell phone, even hands-free, as dangerous as drunk driving according to global workspace theory?
real_qa.r: A 2004 study found that drivers using cell phones, even with hands-free usage, were just as likely to get into car accidents as intoxicated drivers. This is because of global workspace theory, which states that humans can only have one stream of information enter conscious processing at a time. You have the same decreased attention and slower reaction times whether driving drunk or while on the phone.
real_qa.requete: global workspace theory drunk driving cell phone

real_qa.q: How much can multitasking reduce your productivity according to scientific research?
real_qa.r: According to psychologist Gerald Weinberg, multitasking can kill your productivity by up to 80%. However, findings from Dr. David Meyer and Dr. Joshua Rubenstein show a more conservative estimate: productivity will drop up to 40% when you try to multitask. If you completed 10 tasks doing them one at a time, attempting to multitask would result in only getting six of them done.

real_qa.q: What cognitive abilities does frequent multitasking destroy according to Stanford research?
real_qa.r: Stanford research found that people who multitask frequently are worse at filtering information, switching between tasks, and remembering things. Basically, multitasking destroys your ability to be productive.
real_qa.requete: Stanford multitasking cognitive abilities filtering memory

real_qa.q: What is the illusion of progress that prevents leaders from being genuinely productive?
real_qa.r: Many people live their lives with the illusion that they're making progress by spending their days on a treadmill of to-do lists, trying to check off boxes faster than they can add them. When you try to do everything at once by juggling multiple tasks simultaneously, you end up struggling with everything flying in the air while being too busy to realize you aren't being productive at all. Your entire to-do list may simply be an illusion of progress.

real_qa.q: What is the single strategic approach recommended to increase productivity and focus?
real_qa.r: Choose one strategic goal and focus at least one hour per day on that goal and just that goal. Block off your calendar, turn off your notifications, put down your phone, and focus on just that one strategic goal. The secret to success isn't about throwing more balls in the air; it's about recognizing which ones never needed to be tossed up to begin with.
real_qa.requete: single strategic goal focus one task productivity

real_quote: If you try to do everything you end up doing nothing. So stop doing everything and start doing something.
